## Locked design decisions

### D1. Console/stdio sink: minimal TTY server (TX-only), now

A real user-space TTY driver lands in Phase 5 — not a kernel printf shim as
the only console. Scope is deliberately minimal: **TX only, polling PL011**
(write `DR`, poll `FR.TXFF`), no interrupts. The kernel **pre-maps the UART
MMIO page (phys `0x0900_0000`) into TTY's address space at boot** with
Device-nGnRE attributes — TTY is a boot server, so this is a one-off boot
step like stack setup, and `AddrSpace` grows a device-memory mapping mode.
VFS routes fd 1/2 over a new CDEV band to TTY; TTY reads the payload via
grant (`SYS_SAFECOPY`) and writes the UART. Kernel messages keep using the
kernel's own writer; interleaving is acceptable (raw tick bytes already
interleave).

*Rejected:* `SYS_DIAGCTL` as the **only** console (no user-space driver ever
exercised in Phase 5 — but see D2, it still lands as the debug channel);
VM-mediated `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS` device mapping (more MINIX-authentic, revisit
for virtio-mmio in Phase 6); TX+RX with IRQ routing (`SYS_IRQCTL`, GIC → EL0
notification — nothing consumes input until the Phase 7 shell; deferred to
Phase 6 alongside virtio-console).

### D2. `SYS_DIAGCTL` becomes real, early — as the debug channel

Servers currently cannot print at all; every later slice needs observability
while TTY/VFS/grants are still under construction. `SYS_DIAGCTL` (MINIX 3
pedigree: `kernel/system/do_diagctl.c`) gets a body in slice 5.1 with an
**inline-payload** form — length + up to ~90 text bytes inside the 96-byte
message payload — so it needs *zero* user-copy machinery. A `server-rt`
helper loops longer strings. TTY/CDEV is the real stdio path; DIAGCTL is for
server bring-up debugging, exactly like MINIX's kernel message path.

### D3. Root image: MFS image in the MXBI archive + `memory` ramdisk over BDEV

The root filesystem is an **MFS-formatted image** built at compile time by a
new host tool (`tools/mkfs-mfs`), packed into the MXBI archive as a non-ELF
blob (`proc_nr = -1`, name `rootfs`). At boot the kernel **copies the blob
into freshly allocated RAM frames and maps them RW into the `memory`
driver's address space** (the archive copy in kernel `.rodata` stays
pristine; the RAM copy makes the 5.10 write path natural). MEM discovers
`(va, len)` via a new `SYS_GETINFO` selector. MEM serves the image over a
minimal **BDEV band** to MFS. This is the MINIX boot shape (`memory` driver
ramdisk) — Phase 6 swaps virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS.

`tools/mkfs-mfs` is a host Rust binary sharing on-disk structs with the
`fs/mfs` library half, so the format logic is host-tested round-trip
(mkfs writes, mfs reader reads).

*Rejected:* MFS reading the image directly without BDEV (one fewer protocol
now, MFS rework when real block devices arrive); a cpio-style initramfs
unpacked by VFS (avoids MFS entirely — but MFS *is* the Phase 5
deliverable).

### D4. Grant model: real MINIX-style grants — direct + magic — plus `SYS_COPY`

Full MINIX shape, not an interim: each granting process keeps a **grant
table in its own address space** (`GrantEntry` array); `SYS_SETGRANT`
records `(addr, entries)` in the caller's `Priv` (the fields already exist);
`SYS_SAFECOPY` resolves a grant id, reads the entry from the *granter's*
address space, validates (kind, `CPF_READ`/`CPF_WRITE` access, grantee
endpoint, range, idx+seq staleness — MINIX `GRANT_SHIFT` packing), then
copies. Two grant kinds in Phase 5:

- **direct** — granter grants a range of its own memory to a grantee
  (server↔server, e.g. PM→TTY console writes);
- **magic** — a server-grade granter (VFS) grants one process's memory to
  another (TTY/MFS reading a *user's* buffer) — the real single-copy
  read/write data path. Gated on server-grade priv.

**Indirect grants are deferred** (documented `EINVAL` arm) — nothing in
Phase 5 re-grants a received grant.

`SYS_COPY` (raw privileged endpoint+addr copy, MINIX `sys_datacopy`) is
implemented on the same engine — VFS uses it for small control-plane reads
(e.g. fetching a path string from a caller).

**Copy engine + inherent fault safety:** all cross-address-space access goes
through **explicit page-table walks via the HHDM** — the kernel never
dereferences a user VA through the live TTBR0 for grant work. An unmapped
page is a walk miss, returned as `EFAULT`; no exception-fixup machinery
exists or is needed. Page-at-a-time: walk source frame, walk destination
frame, `memcpy` through HHDM aliases. (`AddrSpace` already promises all
table access is HHDM-based and works on non-active address spaces.)

`GrantEntry` is `#[repr(C)]` in `kernel-shared` (flat struct — flags, seq,
grantee, third-party endpoint, addr, len — no union needed for
direct+magic), with the CPF flag constants and id packing helpers,
host-tested.

*Rejected:* direct-only grants (double copy through VFS for every FS byte,
magic retrofitted later anyway); `SYS_COPY`-only interim (ungoverned byte
movement; the chunk-6 brief explicitly prefers real grants).

### D5. Fault-safe user copy: PT-walk replaces `read/write_volatile`

The chunk-6-mandated safety floor, first feature slice (5.1 — right after
the errno resequence so its `EFAULT` marker carries the final value from
day one). The same walk-via-HHDM technique from D4
replaces the two message-copy functions (`copy_msg_from_user` /
`copy_msg_to_user`): a bad user message pointer becomes **`EFAULT` in the
caller's `x0`**, never a panic. The deferred receive-side flush
(`flush_deliver_msg`, currently `let _ =` with a comment admitting the error
is dropped) surfaces failure as `EFAULT` in the *receiver's* parked `x0` —
the receiver asked for delivery to a bad buffer; the message is consumed.
`user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate.

*Rejected:* a real `el1h_sync` handler + ELR fixup table (Linux-style
`extable`) — strictly more machinery for the same observable behavior, and
the PT-walk engine has to exist for grants anyway. Revisit only if message
round-trip cost ever matters (walks can be cached per dispatch).

### D6. ELF authority for FS-backed exec: the kernel keeps it

`boot_image/elf.rs` stays the single ELF loader. It is refactored over a
small **chunked-source abstraction** — read header/phdrs into stack buffers,
copy segment pages — with two sources: the existing boot-image byte slice,
and a **granted user-space buffer** (cross-AS page reads on the D4 engine).
`SYS_EXEC` gains a second payload form carrying `(granter, grant_id, len)`
alongside the existing name form (the name form stays for boot-embedded
regression). PM/VFS stage the file: VFS reads the whole binary from MFS into
a static exec buffer (capped; a compile-time assert covers `/bin/hello`),
direct-grants it to PM's exec flow. No kernel heap, no kernel staging.

The loader stays strict (page-aligned `p_offset`, W^X): user binaries are
linked to comply (see D13). Frame-exhaustion hardening (a `p_memsz` cap)
lands with the grant-source form, since exec input stops being
build-produced.

*Rejected:* a user-space loader in VFS/PM/VM (MINIX-authentic `libexec`
direction — needs map-into-third-party-AS surface through `SYS_VMCTL` and a
second loader implementation for the same milestone; revisit if Phase 7+
wants PIE/interpreters).

### D7. Errno ABI: classic-MINIX values (≡ Linux/musl), MINIX extras above 200

`error.rs` is renumbered once, as the **opening slice (5.0)** — before any C
exists *and* before any Phase 5 slice bakes an errno value into a trace
marker, so no later slice ever re-touches an expected line over a value
change:

- **POSIX block:** classic book-era MINIX values, which are identical to
  Linux/musl numbering for everything Phase 5 needs (EPERM 1 … EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, EINVAL 22, EDEADLK 35, ENOSYS 38 — negated in-kernel as today).
  Where classic MINIX and Linux ever diverge, **musl's value wins** (the
  point is that musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and `syscall_ret.c`'s
  `r > -4096UL` convention work unmodified).

3	//! Fixed-size IPC message.
4	//!
5	//! The 104-byte layout matches MINIX 3's `sizeof(message) == 104` assertion
6	//! for `__x86_64__` (see `include/minix/ipc.h`). Both x86_64 and aarch64 ports
7	//! of minix.rs adopt the same size so that the message is ABI-portable.
8	//!
9	//! Note: MINIX 3 only ever shipped as a 32-bit OS (i386, and 32-bit ARM). The
10	//! `__x86_64__` layout we anchor on exists in the MINIX 3 source tree, but a
11	//! working 64-bit MINIX 3 was never an upstream release — it was a personal
12	//! prototype by this project's author. We treat the 104-byte layout as an ABI
13	//! *reference*, not a shipped 64-bit MINIX 3.
14	//!
15	//! The struct is explicitly 8-aligned. MINIX 3's `message` is a union over
16	//! sub-structs containing `uint64_t` fields, so its native alignment is 8.
17	//! minix.rs expresses `payload` as `[u8; 96]` for now, but future typed
18	//! accessor structs (slice 2.5) will overlay payload regions that contain
19	//! `u64` fields. Forcing the message itself to 8-align guarantees those
20	//! overlays are 8-aligned relative to the message base — required for
21	//! strict-alignment loads on aarch64.
22	//!
23	//! Typed access — MINIX 3 had a union over many `mess_*` payload variants
24	//! (`m1i1`, `m2l1`, etc.). minix.rs will eventually expose strongly-typed
25	//! accessor structs per call (e.g., `as_vfs_read()`), but those live in the
26	//! servers/userland crates so the kernel doesn't pull in every protocol
27	//! definition. For now, `payload` is a raw byte array that callers
28	//! interpret per-call.
29	
30	use crate::endpoint::Endpoint;
31	
32	/// 104-byte fixed-size IPC message. Layout matches MINIX 3 x86_64.
33	#[repr(C, align(8))]
34	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
35	pub struct Message {
36	    /// Endpoint of the sender (set by the kernel on delivery).
37	    pub m_source: Endpoint,
38	    /// Call number on send; result code on reply.
39	    pub m_type: i32,
40	    /// Raw payload — interpreted per-call by typed accessors.
41	    pub payload: [u8; 96],
42	}
43	
44	// Compile-time guarantee that the layout matches MINIX 3's x86_64 message.
45	const _: () = assert!(core::mem::size_of::<Message>() == 104);
46	const _: () = assert!(core::mem::align_of::<Message>() == 8);
47	
48	/// One past the highest user VA reachable through TTBR0. Limine programs
49	/// `TCR_EL1.T0SZ = 16`, giving a 48-bit user VA space (`[0, 2^48)`); the
50	/// kernel's HHDM lives in the very high half via TTBR1 and is unreachable
51	/// from this range.
52	pub const USER_VA_TOP: u64 = 1 << 48;
53	
54	/// Bounds check for a user pointer of length `len` starting at `va`.
55	///
56	/// Rejects:
57	///   - NULL or sub-alignment-of-[`Message`] addresses (a NULL pointer or an
58	///     unaligned `read_volatile` is UB even before the access faults).
59	///   - Pointers whose range extends past [`USER_VA_TOP`].
60	///
61	/// A pure predicate over the message ABI shape, so it lives here (and is
62	/// host-testable) rather than in the kernel's copy helpers.
63	#[inline]
64	pub fn user_va_ok(va: u64, len: usize) -> bool {
65	    if va < core::mem::align_of::<Message>() as u64 {
66	        return false;
67	    }
68	    if !va.is_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<Message>() as u64) {
69	        return false;
70	    }
71	    match va.checked_add(len as u64) {
72	        Some(end) => end <= USER_VA_TOP,
73	        None => false,
74	    }
75	}
76	
77	/// Bounds check for a user *byte buffer* of length `len` starting at `va`.
78	///
79	/// The counterpart of [`user_va_ok`] for ranges that carry no alignment
80	/// requirement — a grant's granted range, or a `SYS_COPY` / `SYS_SAFECOPY`
81	/// buffer, is a plain byte array and may start anywhere. Only the range itself
82	/// is checked: non-NULL, no overflow, and entirely below [`USER_VA_TOP`].
83	///
84	/// Bounding the range is what keeps [`page_chunks`] from being handed an
85	/// attacker-chosen 2^64 length and iterating essentially forever; the mapping
86	/// check is the kernel's page-table walk, not this predicate. A zero length is
87	/// accepted at any non-NULL address (the copy is a no-op).
88	#[inline]
89	pub fn user_range_ok(va: u64, len: u64) -> bool {
90	    if va == 0 {
91	        return false;
92	    }
93	    match va.checked_add(len) {
94	        Some(end) => end <= USER_VA_TOP,
95	        None => false,
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	/// User page granule — the 4 KiB stage-1 granule the kernel's page-table
100	/// walker uses. Declared here (rather than pulled from the kernel's `mmu`
101	/// module) so [`page_chunks`] stays a pure, host-testable helper.
102	pub const USER_PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
103	
104	/// One page-bounded slice of a user buffer, produced by [`page_chunks`].
105	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
106	pub struct PageChunk {
107	    /// Page-aligned base VA of the page holding this chunk.
108	    pub page_va: u64,
109	    /// Byte offset of the chunk within that page.
110	    pub offset: usize,
111	    /// Chunk length. Never crosses the page end, never zero.
112	    pub len: usize,
113	}

115	/// Split the user range `[va, va + len)` into ascending per-page chunks.
116	///
117	/// The kernel's cross-address-space copy engine walks one page-table leaf per
118	/// chunk, so it needs the range decomposed at page boundaries. A 104-byte
119	/// [`Message`] is only 8-aligned, so it genuinely can straddle two pages —
120	/// this is the arithmetic that gets that right.
121	///
122	/// A pure geometry helper over the message ABI shape, so it lives here (and is
123	/// host-testable) rather than in the kernel's copy helpers, alongside
124	/// [`user_va_ok`]. Yields nothing for `len == 0`.
125	#[inline]
126	pub fn page_chunks(va: u64, len: usize) -> PageChunks {
127	    PageChunks { va, remaining: len }
128	}

130	/// Iterator returned by [`page_chunks`].
131	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
132	pub struct PageChunks {
133	    va: u64,
134	    remaining: usize,
135	}

137	impl Iterator for PageChunks {
138	    type Item = PageChunk;

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! minix.rs PM (process manager) server — part A (slice 4.5).
4	//!
5	//! PM owns the POSIX-visible process identity the kernel deliberately knows
6	//! nothing about: pids, parentage, and signal disposition. Part A stands up
7	//! the [`mproc`] table, `getpid`/`getppid` (one `PM_GETPID` call — the reply's
8	//! `m_type` is the pid, payload `0..4` the parent's pid), and the minimal
9	//! kill path: PM drains kernel-queued signals and, with no handlers or masks
10	//! in Phase 4, applies the default disposition — terminate. Fork/exec/wait
11	//! are part B (slice 4.6).
12	//!
13	//! ## The kill chain (all observable kernel-side; EL0 cannot print)
14	//!
15	//! A system process raises a signal with `SYS_KILL` (in 4.5: VM, when a page
16	//! fault lands outside every region — stub D's deliberate SIGSEGV). The
17	//! kernel queues it (`cause_sig`) and wakes PM with a `NOTIFY` from `SYSTEM`;
18	//! [`drain_ksigs`] then loops `SYS_GETKSIG` → disposition → `SYS_ENDKSIG`
19	//! until the kernel reports no more pending procs. Boot servers
20	//! (`MF_PRIV_PROC`) are never terminated — signal-as-message delivery to
21	//! system processes (MINIX's sig2mess) waits for a consumer (RS restarts).
22	//! Every `SYS_GETKSIG`-returned target is `SYS_ENDKSIG`-acknowledged, even
23	//! skipped ones, so no proc is left stranded in signal-pending state; the
24	//! terminate (`SYS_EXIT`) happens *before* the acknowledge so the target
25	//! never becomes runnable in between.
26	//!
27	//! ## Live demo
28	//!
29	//! init (PID 1) is the live process-lifecycle exercise (slice 4.8): a real boot
30	//! process the kernel loader makes runnable, it forks a child, the child execs
31	//! the `worker` binary, and init `wait`s to reap it before looping — driving
32	//! `PM_FORK` / `PM_EXEC` / `PM_WAIT` over the PM ↔ shared-USER-priv edge opened
33	//! by `populate_user_priv`. (This replaced the slice-4.6 frozen stub E, which PM
34	//! used to release via `SYS_PRIVCTL(PRIVCTL_SET_USER)` at SEF init.)
35

# single-char tick bytes, so it must be forced to text). Substrings stop just
# before the first run-variable field (ttbr0_pa / child_e / entry / freed / at);
# nr= values are fixed boot-table slots (kernel-shared/src/com.rs).

[as] ds nr=5 ttbr0_pa=
[as] vfs nr=1 ttbr0_pa=
[as] sched nr=9 ttbr0_pa=
[as] rs nr=2 ttbr0_pa=
[as] pm nr=0 ttbr0_pa=
[as] init nr=10 ttbr0_pa=

[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub B nr=12 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub C nr=13 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub D nr=14 ttbr0_pa=

# fork-pool base, recycled every cycle; exec renames the child to "worker")

[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=worker entry=
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=w nr=15 freed=

# Stub D's designed SIGSEGV chain: page fault -> VM -> SYS_KILL sig=11 -> PM
# tears the stub down with SYS_EXIT
[pf] proc=D far=
[ksys SYS_KILL] target=D nr=14 sig=11 -> pm
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=D nr=14 freed=

# RS's periodic kernel alarm: assert only the FIRST fire (always inside the
# head carve-out) -- timing-robust under slow CI TCG, unlike a fire count
[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=

# of taking an EL1 data abort (which the forbidden list catches as a panic).
# Between them they cover every arm of the copy engine: probe 1 is a fully
# unmapped page, probe 2 straddles A's stack page into the unmapped one above
# it, probe 3 fails in the deferred MF_DELIVERMSG flush and lands EFAULT in A's
# parked x0, and probe 4 names A's *mapped but read-only* code page -- the only
# check on that path is the copy engine's own Prot::writable test, since the
# kernel writes through the HHDM alias where EL0 permission bits do not apply.
# call=1 is SEND; nr=11 is stub A. These lines are unsampled, so unlike
# `[ipc N]` they cannot drift with IPC ordering.

[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x800ff8
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x900000
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x400000

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! minix.rs PM (process manager) server — part A (slice 4.5).
4	//!
5	//! PM owns the POSIX-visible process identity the kernel deliberately knows
6	//! nothing about: pids, parentage, and signal disposition. Part A stands up
7	//! the [`mproc`] table, `getpid`/`getppid` (one `PM_GETPID` call — the reply's
8	//! `m_type` is the pid, payload `0..4` the parent's pid), and the minimal
9	//! kill path: PM drains kernel-queued signals and, with no handlers or masks
10	//! in Phase 4, applies the default disposition — terminate. Fork/exec/wait
11	//! are part B (slice 4.6).
12	//!
13	//! ## The kill chain (all observable kernel-side; EL0 cannot print)
14	//!
15	//! A system process raises a signal with `SYS_KILL` (in 4.5: VM, when a page
16	//! fault lands outside every region — stub D's deliberate SIGSEGV). The
17	//! kernel queues it (`cause_sig`) and wakes PM with a `NOTIFY` from `SYSTEM`;
18	//! [`drain_ksigs`] then loops `SYS_GETKSIG` → disposition → `SYS_ENDKSIG`
19	//! until the kernel reports no more pending procs. Boot servers
20	//! (`MF_PRIV_PROC`) are never terminated — signal-as-message delivery to
21	//! system processes (MINIX's sig2mess) waits for a consumer (RS restarts).
22	//! Every `SYS_GETKSIG`-returned target is `SYS_ENDKSIG`-acknowledged, even
23	//! skipped ones, so no proc is left stranded in signal-pending state; the
24	//! terminate (`SYS_EXIT`) happens *before* the acknowledge so the target
25	//! never becomes runnable in between.
26	//!
27	//! ## Live demo
28	//!
29	//! init (PID 1) is the live process-lifecycle exercise (slice 4.8): a real boot
30	//! process the kernel loader makes runnable, it forks a child, the child execs
31	//! the `worker` binary, and init `wait`s to reap it before looping — driving
32	//! `PM_FORK` / `PM_EXEC` / `PM_WAIT` over the PM ↔ shared-USER-priv edge opened
33	//! by `populate_user_priv`. (This replaced the slice-4.6 frozen stub E, which PM
34	//! used to release via `SYS_PRIVCTL(PRIVCTL_SET_USER)` at SEF init.)
35	
36	// Freestanding for the bare-metal build, but a normal host binary under
37	// `cargo test` so `mproc`'s logic gets host-runnable unit tests. Same gating
38	// as the RS/SCHED servers.
39	#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]
40	#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_main)]
41

47	use minixrs_kernel_shared::Message;
48	use minixrs_kernel_shared::callnr::{
49	    EXEC_NAME_LEN, PM_EXEC, PM_EXIT, PM_FORK, PM_GETPID, PM_GRANT_TEST, PM_WAIT, PRIVCTL_SET_USER,
50	    SAFECOPY_FROM, SAFECOPY_TO, SCHEDULING_START, SCHEDULING_STOP, SYS_COPY, SYS_ENDKSIG, SYS_EXEC,
51	    SYS_EXIT, SYS_FORK, SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN, SYS_GETKSIG, SYS_PRIVCTL, SYS_SAFECOPY, VM_FORK,
52	};
53	use minixrs_kernel_shared::com::{INIT_PROC_NR, SCHED_PROC_NR, SYSTEM, VM_PROC_NR, boot_endpoint};
54	use minixrs_kernel_shared::endpoint::{Endpoint, NONE, SELF, endpoint_proc};
55	use minixrs_kernel_shared::error::{EAGAIN, ECHILD, EFAULT, EINVAL, EPERM, ESRCH, OK};
56	use minixrs_kernel_shared::grant::{CPF_READ, grant_id};

60	/// Priority band and quantum PM assigns a forked child via `SCHEDULING_START`.

64	const CHILD_PRIORITY: i32 = 8;
65	const CHILD_QUANTUM: i32 = 5;

68	/// filesystem/musl wrappers thread a user-supplied path (Phase 5), PM always
69	/// execs the `worker` demo binary — the kernel resolves it by name in the MXBI

71	const EXEC_TARGET: &str = "worker";

84	/// reads them from — the load base every user binary shares (`user.ld`), so
85	/// init's first text page is mapped there for the whole run. The *values* are
86	/// deliberately never asserted: they are init's instruction encodings and change

98	#[cfg_attr(target_os = "none", unsafe(link_section = ".text._start"))]

101	}

104	fn main() -> ! {
105	    // `sef_startup` learns PM's endpoint/name via SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI) and
106	    // runs `pm_init` (DS publish, mproc seed). No signal
107	    // handler: PM *is* the signal manager, not a signal consumer. On failure
108	    // there is nothing to print from EL0 — park forever.

113	    .unwrap_or_else(|_| {

input.new_string:
**Proof:** VFS direct-grants a checksummed buffer at init and publishes the
grant id through DS (`grant.test` key — DS is already a name→i32 registry);
PM retrieves it, `SYS_SAFECOPY`s the buffer, and `diag_print`s the checksum.
Marker line in `qemu-boot.expected`; `[ksys]` traces show the new calls.

**As built** (differences from the sketch above, recorded so later slices do
not rediscover them):

- **The grant id travels in-band, not through DS.** `DS_PUBLISH` deliberately
  registers the kernel-stamped `m_source` and ignores the payload — that is its
  anti-spoof property — so it cannot carry an id at all, and an init-ordering
  handoff through DS would race besides. VFS `ipc_send`s PM a `PM_GRANT_TEST`
  message carrying `{granter, gid, len, rw_gid, addr}` instead. SEND blocks until
  PM's loop receives, so the demo is self-synchronizing; and this is the shape a
  grant id really travels in (slice 5.3's `CDEV_WRITE {minor, granter, grant_id,
  len}` is the same). Cost: one demo-only PM request number (`PM_GRANT_TEST`,
  `NR_PM_MSGS` 5 → 6), to retire when a real consumer lands.
- **The magic arm gets a live QEMU proof**, not just host tests: PM magic-grants
  init's text page (`0x0010_0000`, the load base every user binary shares) to
  itself and safecopies 8 bytes out of init's address space — a genuine
  third-party read from a process that granted nothing. Uses only init's
  endpoint, which PM already holds. Without it the arm would be dead code until
  5.5. The line reports only the length; init's `_start` bytes change on rebuild.
- **`SYS_COPY` is proved in the same exchange**: PM re-reads the *same* bytes
  from VFS's raw address with no grant and compares checksums (`copy ok
  match=1`). That comparison is what proves the grant path moved the right bytes
  rather than merely some bytes.
- **`server-rt` keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.** `GrantPool<const N>` is a
  *value* the server owns (a `main`-frame local that outlives the receive loop),
  not a static — so there is no `UnsafeCell` and no `unsafe impl Sync`. It also

content.content: 185:- **Fault-safe user access + the debug channel (slice 5.1):** the kernel **never dereferences a user VA**, not even the active TTBR0's. Every byte in or out of a user address space goes through `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` — `copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, dst)` / `copy_to_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, src)` / `probe_user_range(ttbr0_pa, va, len, write)` — which page-chunks the range, resolves each page with the new `addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>` (the missing member of the `map_page_in`/`unmap_page_in`/`walk_leaves` free-function family; `AddrSpace::walk_pt` delegates to it), and `memcpy`s through the frame's HHDM alias. Consequences to preserve: an unmapped page is a walk miss returning **`EFAULT`, not an EL1 abort** — so **no exception-fixup table is needed or wanted** (D5 rejected the Linux `extable` approach); the copy is **address-space-independent**, so `flush_deliver_msg` can write a receiver's buffer before its TTBR0 is installed (the TTBR0-before-flush ordering in `sched::schedule_next` is no longer load-bearing, only `eret` needs it); `copy_to_user_as` must **check `Prot::writable`**, because the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping that the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes are **all-or-nothing** (probe first) since a 104-byte `Message` is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages. Slice 5.2's grant engine builds on these primitives rather than re-deriving them. `user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate; the page arithmetic (`page_chunks` / `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE`) lives in `kernel-shared/src/message.rs` beside it because the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`. `ipc/message.rs` carries **zero `unsafe`** — messages stage through a `[u8; 104]` — so all raw-pointer work is in `mm::uaccess` alone. Error routing: `EFAULT` to the caller's `x0` via `do_ipc` for the three immediate sites, and to a blocked receiver's **parked `x0`** (`p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64` — the MINIX `retreg` idiom `do_exit::unblock_dependents` uses) for the deferred flush, which also sets/clears the previously-unused `MF_MSGFAILED`. Both traces are **uncounted** (`[efault] proc=… nr=… call=… va=…`, `[efault deliver] proc=… nr=… va=…`) so they are stable boot markers, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form; the `do_ipc` one keys on `result == EFAULT`, which is unambiguous because nothing else in the kernel produces it. **`SYS_DIAGCTL` is the servers' debug channel** (D2) — servers run at EL0 with no console, and this must keep working while grants/TTY/VFS are under construction, so the text rides **inline in the payload** (subcode `0..4`, len `4..8`, up to `DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88` bytes from `DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8`) and needs no user-copy machinery. `kernel/src/system/do_diagctl.rs` prints one line per call as `[diag <name>] <text>`, where `<name>` is the caller's kernel-known `Proc::name` (never payload data, so a server can only identify itself) and text is sanitized to printable ASCII (so one call is always exactly one line — the `grep -aF` marker contract depends on it). `server-rt::diag_print` is the client, chunking longer strings; it is called from **`sef_startup`**, so all six SEF servers emit `[diag <name>] sef ready` at boot. Adding a stub is discouraged: `NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE`, so a fifth stub shifts init's forked children 15 → 16 and breaks checked-in markers — put new probe behavior in an existing stub's prologue (5.1 used stub A's)

1	# minix.rs
2	
3	minix.rs — "MINIX 3, in Rust, for the 64-bit era" — is a 64-bit-only reimplementation of MINIX 3 in Rust, preserving the original ABI. It is a learning OS built around a greenfield Rust microkernel.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	- **Kernel:** Rust (no_std, no_main), greenfield microkernel
8	- **Architecture:** aarch64 primary (Apple Silicon / QEMU virt), x86_64 secondary
9	- **Servers:** PM, VFS, VM, RS, DS, SCHED as user-space Rust processes
10	- **Drivers:** VirtIO (MMIO for aarch64, PCI for x86_64) as user-space processes
11	- **C library:** musl-libc fork with MINIX IPC syscall wrappers
12	- **License:** BSD-3-Clause only (no GPL code)
13	- **Platform:** QEMU as primary target
14	
15	## Reference Codebase
16	
17	minix.rs's architecture is based on MINIX 3. When the docs reference "MINIX 3 source",
18	they mean paths within the MINIX 3 source tree (e.g., `kernel/proc.c` means the
19	`kernel/proc.c` file in a MINIX 3 checkout). Key reference files:
20	
21	- `kernel/proc.c` -- IPC implementation (mini_send, mini_receive, deadlock detection)
22	- `kernel/proc.h`, `priv.h` -- Process and privilege structures
23	- `kernel/system.c` -- Kernel call dispatch
24	- `include/minix/ipc.h` -- Message structure definitions
25	- `include/minix/com.h`, `callnr.h` -- Server endpoints, call numbers
26	- `sys/sys/errno.h` -- errno values. Modern MINIX 3 keeps the MINIX-specific band (200+)
27	  here under the NetBSD layout, *not* in `include/errno.h`; the classic book-era tree has
28	  everything in `include/errno.h`
29	- `lib/libc/sys/*.c` -- POSIX syscall wrappers (template for musl adaptation)
30	- `lib/libsys/sef.c` -- SEF framework (template for server-rt)
31	
32	The MINIX 3 source is available at https://github.com/Stichting-MINIX-Research-Foundation/minix
33	
34	## Build
35	
36	```sh
37	# Build kernel for aarch64 (primary target)
38	cargo kernel-aarch64
39	
40	# Boot in QEMU (cargo runner wires tools/qemu-run.sh). The kernel runs
41	# indefinitely once EL0 starts (slice 2.4+), so `timeout` is mandatory.
42	# Redirect to a file when you need to grep tick output -- live tail loses lines.
43	# The log interleaves raw single-char tick bytes; grep it with `grep -a`
44	# (force text) or matches read as "Binary file matches".
45	# Budget ~5 s of every run for the cargo rebuild + UEFI firmware startup before
46	# the kernel's first byte: `timeout 8` yields a log with NO kernel output at all
47	# (check-boot-log.sh then fails all 24 markers). Use 25 s for anything you mean
48	# to verify. QEMU under TCG also advances *guest* time slower than wall-clock, so
49	# a `timeout N` run reaches far fewer than N x 100 ticks. For time-based features
50	# (alarms, quantum/scheduling) read uptime-stamped traces (e.g. `[alarm ... at=N]`)
51	# as the real clock, and run 20-25 s to observe several periods.
52	timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release
53	
54	# Clean, stub-free boot for debugging (servers + init/worker only, no demo
55	# stubs A-D): add --no-default-features to disable the `boot-stubs` feature.
56	timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release --no-default-features
57	
58	# Verify a captured boot log against the standard acceptance markers:
59	#   tools/check-boot-log.sh <log>   (tests/qemu-boot.expected/.forbidden;
60	# update those marker files in the same PR when trace formats or the boot
61	# roster change, or the qemu-smoke CI job goes red)
62	
63	# (There is no `kernel-x86_64` alias: `forced-target` pins the kernel to
64	# aarch64, so such an alias would silently build aarch64 instead of failing.
65	# x86_64 is Phase 8 -- there is no kernel/src/arch/x86_64/ yet either.)
66	
67	# Run host-side unit tests (note the package name, not the dir name)
68	cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared
69	cargo test -p minixrs-gen-c-headers
70	
71	# Regenerate the C ABI headers for the musl fork (slice 5.0). Output is a build
72	# artifact under target/ and is NEVER committed; `--stdout` dumps it instead.
73	cargo gen-c-headers
74	```

content.text:
Slice 5.2 is implemented and verified. Everything in the plan landed, plus a few things the verification steps forced.

## What's in

**`kernel-shared`** — new `grant.rs`: flat `#[repr(C)] GrantEntry` (32 B, layout pinned by `offset_of!` asserts since the kernel decodes it from raw bytes), MINIX's CPF flag values, `GRANT_SHIFT = 20` id packing. `message.rs` gains `dual_page_chunks` and `user_range_ok`. `callnr.rs` gains `SAFECOPY_FROM`/`_TO`, `PM_GRANT_TEST`, `NR_PM_MSGS` 5→6. 68 → 91 tests.

**Kernel** — `mm::uaccess::copy_between_as` (probe both, walk-and-memcpy per dual chunk, all-or-nothing); `do_setgrant.rs` / `do_safecopy.rs` / `do_copy.rs` replacing the three `ENOSYS` stubs, all routed from the target-taking `match`; `do_exit` clears a dedicated priv's grant registration.

**`server-rt`** — `GrantPool<const N>` as an owned value, so `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; pure `*_in` helpers with 14 host tests.

**Demo** — VFS direct-grants PM a checksummed `.rodata` buffer, PM reads it three ways (grant / raw `SYS_COPY` / magic read of init's text page) and runs seven denial probes.

## Deviations worth flagging

- **`user_range_ok` is new** (not in the plan). `user_va_ok` demands 8-alignment, which is right for the grant table but wrong for the byte buffers `SYS_SAFECOPY`/`SYS_COPY` move — and something has to bound `len` before `page_chunks` sees it.
- **Seven denial probes instead of an implicit mutation exercise.** The plan asked for mutation checks; leaving them as a one-off run means the validators go back to being unexercised. `[diag pm] grant.deny ok n=7` keeps grantee / access / seq / idx / range / lying-`CPF_WRITE`-over-`.rodata` / unmapped-page permanently covered by a boot marker. That needed VFS to issue a second, deliberately-lying `CPF_READ|CPF_WRITE` grant over the same read-only buffer.
- **Two validators are not independently observable**, and I recorded why rather than papering over it: an out-of-range grant index is caught by the entry read failing first, and the `SYS_PROC` magic gate has no possible negative case yet — every process that can call `SYS_SETGRANT` is server-grade. I proved the gate is live by inverting it (`magic ok` → `magic FAIL rc=-1`) instead.
- **Kind selection is an exact mask match**, so an entry claiming two kinds is `EINVAL` rather than falling into the more permissive branch.

## Verification

`fmt --check`, all three clippy gates, 29 test suites (0 failures), `gen-c-headers` + `clang -fsyntax-only` on all three triples and the opt-in errno block — all green. QEMU: 38/38 markers, forbidden list clean. Stub-free boot: no `[efault]`, demo still fires.

Mutation-tested one at a time: removing the grantee, seq, access, or range check, or `copy_between_as`'s destination-writable probe, each flips `grant.deny ok` to `FAIL <name>`. All mutations reverted; the tree is back to the shipped state.

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! minix.rs PM (process manager) server — part A (slice 4.5).
4	//!
5	//! PM owns the POSIX-visible process identity the kernel deliberately knows
6	//! nothing about: pids, parentage, and signal disposition. Part A stands up
7	//! the [`mproc`] table, `getpid`/`getppid` (one `PM_GETPID` call — the reply's
8	//! `m_type` is the pid, payload `0..4` the parent's pid), and the minimal
9	//! kill path: PM drains kernel-queued signals and, with no handlers or masks
10	//! in Phase 4, applies the default disposition — terminate. Fork/exec/wait
11	//! are part B (slice 4.6).
12	//!
13	//! ## The kill chain (all observable kernel-side; EL0 cannot print)
14	//!
15	//! A system process raises a signal with `SYS_KILL` (in 4.5: VM, when a page
16	//! fault lands outside every region — stub D's deliberate SIGSEGV). The
17	//! kernel queues it (`cause_sig`) and wakes PM with a `NOTIFY` from `SYSTEM`;
18	//! [`drain_ksigs`] then loops `SYS_GETKSIG` → disposition → `SYS_ENDKSIG`
19	//! until the kernel reports no more pending procs. Boot servers
20	//! (`MF_PRIV_PROC`) are never terminated — signal-as-message delivery to
21	//! system processes (MINIX's sig2mess) waits for a consumer (RS restarts).
22	//! Every `SYS_GETKSIG`-returned target is `SYS_ENDKSIG`-acknowledged, even
23	//! skipped ones, so no proc is left stranded in signal-pending state; the
24	//! terminate (`SYS_EXIT`) happens *before* the acknowledge so the target
25	//! never becomes runnable in between.
26	//!
27	//! ## Live demo
28	//!
29	//! init (PID 1) is the live process-lifecycle exercise (slice 4.8): a real boot
30	//! process the kernel loader makes runnable, it forks a child, the child execs
31	//! the `worker` binary, and init `wait`s to reap it before looping — driving
32	//! `PM_FORK` / `PM_EXEC` / `PM_WAIT` over the PM ↔ shared-USER-priv edge opened
33	//! by `populate_user_priv`. (This replaced the slice-4.6 frozen stub E, which PM
34	//! used to release via `SYS_PRIVCTL(PRIVCTL_SET_USER)` at SEF init.)
35	
36	// Freestanding for the bare-metal build, but a normal host binary under
37	// `cargo test` so `mproc`'s logic gets host-runnable unit tests. Same gating
38	// as the RS/SCHED servers.
39	#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]
40	#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_main)]

42	mod mproc;

47	use minixrs_kernel_shared::Message;
48	use minixrs_kernel_shared::callnr::{

52	};
53	use minixrs_kernel_shared::com::{
54	    INIT_PROC_NR, SCHED_PROC_NR, SYSTEM, VFS_PROC_NR, VM_PROC_NR, boot_endpoint,
55	};
56	use minixrs_kernel_shared::endpoint::{Endpoint, NONE, SELF, endpoint_proc};

61	
62	/// Priority band and quantum PM assigns a forked child via `SCHEDULING_START`.
63	/// These match SCHED's own `USER_Q` / `QUANTUM` (`servers/sched/src/policy.rs`)
64	/// so a child round-robins in the managed band rather than sinking behind the
65	/// kernel-scheduled stubs.
66	const CHILD_PRIORITY: i32 = 8;

82	/// the pool costs `N * 32` bytes; the demo issues one magic grant at a time.
83	const GRANT_SLOTS: usize = 8;

86	/// reads them from — the load base every user binary shares (`user.ld`), so

content.text:
All five findings were valid and are fixed. Verified re-green: fmt, three clippy gates, 29 test suites, `gen-c-headers` + clang on all three triples, 38/38 QEMU markers, stub-free boot clean.

## 1. PM confused deputy — real, fixed

The sharpest of the five. PM holds `SYS_COPY`/`SYS_SAFECOPY`; its clients (init, every forked child on the shared USER privilege) hold neither. A payload-supplied granter meant any of them could aim a privileged cross-AS copy at a third party through PM and read a checksum of the result off the console.

Fix is the DS lesson applied properly: **the granter is now `msg.m_source`**, and the granter field is gone from the payload entirely — layout is now `{gid, len, rw_gid, addr}`. A client can only ever name its own address space. PM additionally serves the arm only when `m_source` is VFS. The boot log confirms the substitution works end to end: `[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=1` now comes from the kernel stamp.

I recorded this in `CLAUDE.md` and the As-built notes as a rule binding slice 5.3+ — CDEV/BDEV/FS must not reintroduce a payload granter field.

## 2. `do_exec` grant leak — real, fixed

exec preserves the privilege slot while replacing the address space, so `grant_table` survived pointing at a VA that now belongs to the new image. `do_exec` takes `priv_table` and clears the registration at the point of no return, guarded by the same `proc_nr == Some(target)` dedicated-slot test `do_exit` uses.

One thing worth being straight about: **this arm is unreachable in today's boot.** The only exec'ing procs are init's forked children on the shared `USER_PRIV_ID`, which the guard skips. It goes live the first time a server execs. I've said so in the As-built notes rather than implying it's covered by a marker.

## 3. `revoke` and the moved pool — real, fixed

I'd underweighted this. A grant that goes stale is benign (garbage fails `CPF_USED`); a **revoke** that silently doesn't reach the kernel is not — the entry gets cleared in the moved pool while the kernel keeps honouring the old address. `revoke` now calls `ensure_registered` first, with an early-out when nothing was ever registered so `new()`'s "no kernel calls until the first grant" property holds.

## 4 & 5. Both mine, both fixed

The "five denials" comment predated the rodata and unmapped probes — now says seven and explains why two are `EFAULT` rather than `EPERM`. The `PM_GRANT_TEST` doc was rewritten for the new layout and now documents `rw_gid` plus the m_source rule and why it exists.

Still uncommitted on `feature/slice-5.2-grants`.

git commit -F - <<'MSG'
Slice 5.2: grant table + SYS_SETGRANT / SYS_SAFECOPY / SYS_COPY

Implements decision D4's grant model, live end to end between two boot
servers. A granting process keeps its GrantEntry table in its own address
space and registers (addr, entries) with SYS_SETGRANT; SYS_SAFECOPY reads
the entry back out of the granter's address space on every call, so a
granter revokes by writing its own memory and the kernel caches nothing
that could go stale.

kernel-shared: new grant.rs — flat #[repr(C)] GrantEntry (32 B, layout
pinned by offset_of! asserts since the kernel decodes it from raw bytes),
MINIX's CPF flag values, GRANT_SHIFT = 20 id packing. message.rs gains
dual_page_chunks and user_range_ok (a granted range is a byte buffer and
need not be 8-aligned, so user_va_ok is the wrong gate; bounding the range
is also what stops page_chunks being handed a 2^64 length). callnr.rs
gains SAFECOPY_FROM/_TO, PM_GRANT_TEST, NR_PM_MSGS 5 -> 6. 68 -> 91 tests.

Kernel: mm::uaccess::copy_between_as — probe both ranges, then walk and
memcpy per dual chunk. All-or-nothing on the destination, and its
Prot::writable check is load-bearing: a granter may lie about writability
and the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 bits do not police.
do_setgrant / do_safecopy / do_copy replace the three ENOSYS stubs, routed
from the target-taking match (SYS_SETGRANT included — caller-local in
effect but it needs &mut Priv). verify_grant validates in MINIX's order and
hides a granter-side walk miss as EPERM so a grantee cannot probe the
granter's address space; CPF_MAGIC is gated on Priv::flags & SYS_PROC,
CPF_INDIRECT is a documented EINVAL, and kind selection is an exact mask
match so an entry claiming two kinds is malformed rather than permissive.
do_exit and do_exec both clear a dedicated slot's registration — exit so a
recycled slot cannot inherit a stale table address, exec because the
registered VA describes the image being discarded while the privilege slot
survives.

server-rt: GrantPool<const N> is a value the server owns, not a static,
which is what keeps the crate #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. ensure_registered
compares the pool's live address against the last registered one, so a
moved pool re-registers rather than leaving the kernel pointed at freed
stack; revoke re-registers too, since clearing a slot only revokes
anything if the kernel is reading that copy of the table.

Demo: VFS direct-grants PM a checksummed .rodata buffer and hands the id
over in-band (DS cannot carry one — DS_PUBLISH registers m_source and
ignores the payload, which is precisely its anti-spoof property). PM reads
it through the grant, re-reads the same bytes with the ungranted SYS_COPY
and compares checksums, and magic-grants itself init's text page for a
genuine third-party read. The granter is taken from the kernel-stamped
m_source, never the payload: PM holds SYS_COPY/SYS_SAFECOPY and its clients
do not, so a caller-supplied granter would make PM a confused deputy.

Seven denial probes ([diag pm] grant.deny ok n=7) keep every validator
exercised by a boot marker — wrong grantee, wrong access, stale sequence,
out-of-range index, range overrun, a granter lying about writability, and
a grant over an unmapped page. Mutation-tested one at a time: removing the
grantee, seq, access, or range check, or copy_between_as's
destination-writable probe, each flips the line to FAIL. Two findings
recorded rather than papered over: the index range check is not
independently observable (the out-of-table read fails first), and the
SYS_PROC magic gate cannot be probed at all yet because every process able
to call SYS_SETGRANT is server-grade — inverting it proved it live instead.

Verification: fmt, all three clippy gates, 29 test suites, gen-c-headers +
clang -fsyntax-only on three triples, 38/38 QEMU markers, and a stub-free
boot with no [efault] lines.
